_about: Per-operation perf budgets in nanoseconds for the C# implementation. measured = `make perf-baseline-csharp` (dotnet run -c Release --project csharp/perf/Provide.Telemetry.Perf -- --iterations 300000 --runs 5 --emit-json). baseline_ns is the median of the runner's own per-run medians across seven consecutive invocations; tolerance_multiplier sets the budget = baseline_ns * tolerance_multiplier. Uniform 5.0 as in perf-go.json and perf-rust.json. The runner disables tiered compilation, which makes it the most reproducible of the five: those seven invocations spread only 1.10x-1.14x on every op, on a host that was running other work at the time. 5.0 is therefore not a fit to the observed noise but the house convention, kept because this bucket was seeded on a 16-core developer workstation (.NET 10.0.302) rather than on the ubuntu-latest runner it will be compared against, and different hardware can legitimately differ by 2x. Reseed from a CI log and tightening toward 3.0 becomes defensible. macos-arm64 and windows-x86_64 are intentionally empty: perf_check.py exits 0 with a hint for a missing bucket, so the first CI run on those runners prints the numbers to paste in.
